sections.overview: The sharptail mola is a large oceanic sunfish in the family Molidae and the sole living member of Masturus; it is related to but distinct from the ocean sunfish Mola mola.
sections.identification: Its tall, flattened body ends in a truncated tail-like clavus with a central pointed projection, unlike the unpointed clavus of Mola mola; it can approach three metres long.
sections.habitat: It occurs in tropical and warm-temperate waters of the major oceans, although its scattered records leave its full distribution imperfectly known.
sections.diet: A recent diet study found varied prey, with tunicates prominent in sampled fish and prey drawn from several ocean depths and habitats.
sections.behavior: It is rarely observed directly, though tagging has documented deep dives whose purpose remains uncertain.
sections.reproduction: Its breeding season and reproductive biology remain poorly known.
sections.ecology: It occupies open-water food webs and is targeted in a Taiwanese fishery where megamouth sharks are also caught incidentally; see that shark’s profile for the reciprocal link.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment published in 2015 classified it as Least Concern but noted uncertainty and the need for better catch and biological data.
